newsitem.title: UK: Dlr ignored, Fr franc takes centre stage in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Dlr ignored, Fr franc takes centre stage in Europe.

text.p: The European forex market was calmer in late business, with all eyes still on mark/Paris and only scant attention paid to dollar/mark and dollar/yen.
But even on mark/Paris, attention was tending to wane and traders were taking profits after perceived Bank of France intervention.
The mark was trading around 3.4257/62 French francs, back from an early five-month high of 3.4296. Traders said Bank of Francesold marks at 3.4295.
The dollar was at 1.4810/15 marks and 108.40/45 yen, with dollar/mark up on Wednesday's 1.4760/63 but dollar/yen steady.
Analysts said the light profit taking on mark/French franc positions did not mean that the market will not test the upside again sometime soon, but it may require a catalyst.

"I think a lot of people have got a (mark/Paris) position already," said David Coleman, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy. "Everyone knows the rumours and the theories, what we need now is some proper facts, not just talk. That will be the next step in this mini-crisis the franc is having."
The franc is being hit by worries over European monetary union as the 1997 French budget looms and as the threat of widespread strike action hangs over the country.
French trade union leader Marc Blondel today joined a chorus of union voices predicting a tough autumn for the government.
The worry for the market is that the government will not be able to square the circle of tightening fiscal policy in order to meet the Maastricht critera with getting the weak economy to pick up.

Public resistance to such austerity will also be a problem with French unemployment data for June on Friday expected to equal June's record high of 12.5 percent. The dollar was helped higher versus the mark by an unexpected upward revision to U.S. Q2 GDP.
GDP was revised up to 4.8 percent in the second quarter from an original 4.2 percent with the price index revised up to 2.2 percent against 2.1 percent.

New home sales were also stronger than expected. "The home sales showed the largest rise in five months and does not suggest that there is any significant slowdown in the housing market," said Jeremy Hawkins, senior economic adviser at BankAmerica.
"The data adds to the worries generated by the GDP report that the economy is growing at a pace that is not sustainable and will cause the Fed to tighten to slow the pace of activity."

There is plenty of Japanese data overnight with CPI, consumer prices, unemployment and industrial production all due. The weaker than expected Tankan survey earlier this week dampened speculation of a near-term rise in Japanese interest rates and Friday's batch of data will be closely watched for signs of strength, dealers said. Phil Smith, London Forex desk +44-171-542-6284.
